value.notes: Per the County's own Electrical Permit and Inspection Section page: 'The electrical permit will be issued within 30 days after the application is deemed complete.'

other_conditions: Roof-mounted PV: an electrical permit is always required; a BUILDING permit is required ONLY IF the licensed architect/structural engineer determines the existing roof truss system cannot support the added weight without additional structural reinforcing — otherwise no building permit is needed for the PV system itself
A C-13 licensed electrical contractor is required to obtain the electrical permit; the electrical contractor is responsible for PV system design and installation
Free-standing (ground-mounted) PV systems always require BOTH a building permit and an electrical permit, with scaled/detailed site, foundation, elevation, framing, and mounting plans
PV systems rated 30 kW or more require schematics prepared, stamped, and signed by a Hawaii-licensed electrical engineer (not just an architect/structural engineer letter)

PV systems are allowed on buildings exempt from a building permit under Maui County Code 16.26.106.2 exemptions 1 and 16, but are NOT allowed on structures that were illegally constructed without a required building permit

Electrical permits expire if the initial required inspection is not approved within 1 year of issuance; once the initial inspection is approved, the permit remains active up to 5 years from issuance or until final inspection, whichever occurs first
Permits for photovoltaic systems may require a separate Fire Permit from the Fire Prevention Bureau

permit_fees.notes: The County's own page states electrical permit fees 'are based on the size and quantities of the installation and are set by budget ordinance' but does not publish the specific fee schedule/table on this page; the referenced budget ordinance was not independently located and read this session.
